props.gloss_en: one suspect regarding the Sabbatical Year is not suspect regarding tithes
one suspect regarding tithes is not suspect regarding the Sabbatical Year
and there is one who is suspect regarding ritually pure items and is suspect neither regarding this nor that
what is the reason? granted he is suspect regarding rabbinic law; regarding Torah law he is not suspect
the baraita: one trusted regarding ritually pure items is trusted regarding the Sabbatical Year
the inference from the baraita: then one suspect [regarding purity] is suspect [regarding the Sabbatical Year]
R' Ilai: our mishna is where they saw him conduct himself privately within his house
R' Yannai b'R' Yishmael: [the baraita is] where he was suspect regarding both, came before the Rabbis and accepted both, and was then suspected again regarding one of them
for we say: since he is suspect regarding this one, he is suspect regarding the other too
version 1: this [clause, one suspect on shviit is not suspect on tithe] is the view of R' Akiva, the unattributed
but the Sages say: one suspect regarding the Sabbatical Year is suspect regarding tithe
who are the Sages [who say shviit -> tithe]? R' Yehuda
for in R' Yehuda's locale the Sabbatical Year was stringent for them
as that man who called his fellow 'convert son of a convert' -- [the other] said to him: [a blessing] come to me, for I do not eat Sabbatical-Year produce like you
version 2: this [clause, one suspect on tithe is not suspect on shviit] is the view of R' Akiva, the unattributed
but the Sages say: one suspect regarding tithe is suspect regarding the Sabbatical Year
and who are the Sages [who say tithe -> shviit]? it is R' Meir
R' Meir: one suspect regarding one matter is suspect regarding the entire Torah
an am haaretz who accepted upon himself the duties of a chaver and was suspected regarding one matter is suspected regarding the entire Torah -- R' Meir
and the Sages say: he is suspected only regarding that matter alone
a convert who accepted upon himself the words of Torah, even if suspected regarding one matter, is suspect regarding the entire Torah
and he is like an apostate Israelite
the practical difference: if he betroths, his betrothal is a betrothal
one who comes to accept the duties of a chaver except for one matter is not accepted
a gentile who comes to accept the words of Torah except for one matter is not accepted
R' Yosei b'R' Yehuda: even [excepting] one fine point of the words of the Scribes [he is not accepted]
and so a Levite who comes to accept the duties of Levites, and a priest who comes to accept the duties of priesthood, except for one matter, is not accepted
as it is said: 'he who offers the blood of the peace offerings [and the fat, of the sons of Aaron, shall have the right thigh for a portion]'
the service handed over to the sons of Aaron: any priest who does not acknowledge it has no share in the priesthood
one who comes to accept the duties of a chaver: if we saw him conduct himself privately within his house, he is accepted and afterwards taught
and if not, he is taught and afterwards accepted
RSbY: either way he is accepted, and he goes on learning in his way
